description: We are MapWay, a multidisciplinary team of six innovators combining aerospace engineering, software development, UI/UX design, geospatial data analytics, and technical science writing. Our crew—Oleg Zuban, Sofiia Yachmenova, Katherine Rogachova, Taisiia Zherlitsyna, Arkhyp Onyshchenko, and Dmitrii Aleksandrov—came together with a shared mission: turning complex planetary science datasets into actionable, human-centered survival tools for the first explorers of the Red Planet. By uniting hardware-informed operational logic with modern interactive web technologies, we bridge the gap between raw orbital telemetry and real-time astronaut decision-making
summary: Interplanetary Survival Guide: The Martian Map is an integrated, three-part mission-planning and survival ecosystem built around our MapWay Web-GIS platform, the Red Horizon 120-sol interactive survival simulator, and a comprehensive tactical Survival Manual. Because round-trip radio communication between Earth and Mars suffers a 6-to-44-minute delay and periodic solar conjunction blackouts, astronauts cannot rely on real-time Mission Control during emergencies. Our solution fuses multi-layered NASA and USGS topographic, hazard, and subsurface ice datasets with predictive AI decision support and scenario-based training to transform passive users into "Mars Ready" explorers capable of safely landing, navigating, and sustaining an autonomous base.
details:
Interplanetary Survival Guide: The Martian Map addresses a fundamental operational bottleneck of human Mars exploration: the absence of real-time assistance from Earth. With one-way signal latency ranging from 3 to 22 minutes (6 to 44 minutes round-trip) depending on orbital mechanics, plus communication blackouts when solar activity or planetary alignment obstructs the line of sight, Martian crews must operate with high autonomy. Our project solves this by integrating three interconnected components into a browser-accessible, zero-install ecosystem:

  1. MapWay Web-GIS Cartographic Engine: An interactive, multi-layered Martian mapping tool built with Martian coordinate referencing. Users toggle between elevation layers, hazard zones (steep slopes, impact craters, boulder fields, and unstable dunes), subsurface water-ice probability layers concentrated in the 40°–55° N mid-latitude belt, and solar illumination profiles. Using a multi-criteria weighted evaluation model, MapWay compares candidate regions—demonstrating why smooth, ice-rich Utopia Planitia (46°N, 122°E; score 4.10/5) is optimal for a primary human base, whereas rugged, biosignature-rich Jezero Crater (18°N, 77°E; score 3.55/5) is best suited as a robotic scientific outpost. The route planner also calculates slope-weighted rover energy expenditure and terrain entrapment risk calibrated against historical NASA rover mobility logs.
  2. Red Horizon Sim (120-Sol Interactive Survival Simulator): A turn-based web and mobile survival game where players command a six-person expedition across 120 Martian sols. Players select a landing site, configure spacecraft payload mass and budget, and construct a closed-loop base utilizing In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU)—including Rodwell subsurface ice drills, perchlorate water filtration, MOXIE-inspired atmospheric CO₂-to-oxygen conversion, Kilopower fission reactors paired with solar arrays, hydroponic greenhouses, and regolith radiation shielding. Throughout the mission, players manage 0.38g musculoskeletal countermeasures (ROCKY resistance equipment and Gravity Suits) and respond to dynamic crises such as dust storms, solar proton flares, equipment failures, and medical emergencies, assisted by a predictive AI advisory layer that forecasts resource deficits and environmental hazards.
  3. Interplanetary Survival Manual & "Mars Ready" Framework: A structured operational handbook covering Martian geography, closed-loop life support, space medicine, crew psychology, international space law (Outer Space Treaty and COSPAR planetary protection guidelines), and step-by-step emergency protocols alongside self-assessment drills.

Developed using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, SVG vector mapping, and open GIS workflows, the entire platform runs directly in desktop and mobile browsers without installation and is permanently hosted on GitHub and Google Drive for open judge and public use.
